questions.stem: Which sequence matches CLZ-120's first Azure deployment workflow?

options.A: Initialize, format-check, validate, plan, inspect, apply, verify.
options.B: Apply, initialize, inspect, validate.
options.C: Destroy, apply, then choose a subscription.
options.D: Format, verify Azure, then skip planning.

optionExplanations.A: Inspection precedes execution and validation follows deployment.
optionExplanations.B: Initialization and review should happen before apply.
optionExplanations.C: Target context must be established first.
optionExplanations.D: The lab explicitly requires reviewing the proposed changes.

questions.stem: What Azure object does the supplied CLZ-120 module deploy?

options.A: A Windows VM and disk.
options.B: One tagged resource group.
options.C: An Azure Storage remote backend.

optionExplanations.A: Compute starts in a later lesson.
optionExplanations.B: This is the smallest managed boundary used for the lifecycle exercise.
optionExplanations.C: This lesson uses local state.
optionExplanations.D: Networking starts later.

questions.stem: Which command reviews the exact tfplan file before execution?

options.A: terraform fmt tfplan
options.B: az group show tfplan
options.C: terraform show tfplan

optionExplanations.A: Fmt handles configuration, not binary plans.
optionExplanations.B: Azure CLI does not read plan files.
optionExplanations.C: Show displays the saved plan.
optionExplanations.D: A plan file is not a managed address.

questions.stem: How does the lesson apply the saved changes already inspected by the learner?

options.A: terraform apply -out tfplan
options.B: terraform output tfplan
options.C: terraform validate tfplan

optionExplanations.A: -out is a plan-saving option, not this apply syntax.
optionExplanations.B: Output reads stored results.
optionExplanations.C: Validate is not plan execution.
optionExplanations.D: Providing the file executes that saved plan.

questions.stem: Why pass subscription_id explicitly while Azure CLI supplies authentication?

options.A: To pin the deployment target to the intended subscription.
options.B: To create a new Azure subscription.
options.C: To increase regional quota.

optionExplanations.A: Identity and target selection are complementary controls.
optionExplanations.B: This module creates a resource group only.
optionExplanations.C: A subscription input does not change quota.
optionExplanations.D: State remains part of Terraform's lifecycle.

questions.stem: Which cost statement fits CLZ-120?

options.A: Tags remove the cost of any future VM.
options.B: The empty group has no direct charge; contained services may be billable.
options.C: The group costs the same as a running VM.

optionExplanations.A: Tags do not waive service charges.
optionExplanations.B: Resource groups are management containers.
optionExplanations.C: A group is not compute.
optionExplanations.D: State location does not cancel resource charges.

questions.stem: After apply, which evidence confirms the resource group's actual Azure properties?

options.A: The success of terraform fmt alone.
options.B: The filename resource-group.tf.
options.C: az group show using the Terraform output name.
options.D: A saved plan from before apply.

optionExplanations.A: Formatting does not query deployment state.
optionExplanations.B: A source filename is not deployment evidence.
optionExplanations.C: It reads the deployed object from Azure.
optionExplanations.D: A proposal is not actual Azure readback.

sources.title: Manage resource groups with Azure CLI

questions.stem: Which address should terraform state list contain for this lesson?

options.A: resource_group_name
options.B: local.tags
options.C: subscription_id

optionExplanations.A: That is an output, not the resource address.
optionExplanations.B: A local expression is not managed state inventory.
optionExplanations.C: An input is not a managed Azure resource.
optionExplanations.D: The resource type and local name form its address.

questions.stem: A second plan after successful CLZ-120 apply reports no changes. What does that support?

options.A: The managed object matches the evaluated configuration.
options.B: All resources in the subscription are managed.
options.C: Future drift is impossible.

optionExplanations.A: It is a useful convergence check at that time.
optionExplanations.B: This module tracks only its declared object.
optionExplanations.C: Later out-of-band changes can still occur.
optionExplanations.D: An empty normal plan is not a destroy.

questions.stem: A learner changes environment so the derived resource-group name changes. What must be reviewed?

options.A: Only the console's text color.
options.B: Any destroy/create replacement shown by the plan.
options.C: An automatic subscription move.

optionExplanations.A: Appearance is unrelated to resource replacement.
optionExplanations.B: A name change can alter the managed object's identity.
optionExplanations.C: The environment input does not select another subscription.
optionExplanations.D: The derived name changes too.

questions.stem: Where should the learner place actual local values copied from terraform.tfvars.example?

options.A: In a public GitHub comment.
options.B: Inside every resource block.
options.C: In the untracked terraform.tfvars file.
options.D: In the README's shared deployment example.

optionExplanations.A: That unnecessarily publishes deployment context.
optionExplanations.B: Duplicating inputs makes configuration harder to maintain.
optionExplanations.C: The example is a template; personal values stay out of source control.
optionExplanations.D: Shared examples should preserve placeholders.

questions.stem: Why initialize with -lockfile=readonly during the lesson?

options.A: To forbid future Azure writes.
options.B: To remove the backend state lock.
options.C: To skip provider installation entirely.
options.D: To use the committed provider dependency choices without rewriting them.

optionExplanations.A: The flag controls dependency-file changes only.
optionExplanations.B: Dependency locking and state locking differ.
optionExplanations.C: Initialization may still install the selected provider.
optionExplanations.D: This helps keep the reviewed dependency selection stable.

questions.stem: The first Azure plan returns an authorization error. Which action fits CLZ-120 troubleshooting?

options.A: Verify the role at the intended scope and allow new grants to propagate.
options.B: Change the environment tag to prod.
options.C: Run apply repeatedly without reading the failure.

optionExplanations.A: The provider needs authorized access, not just valid syntax.
optionExplanations.B: Labels do not grant permissions.
optionExplanations.C: Repeated execution does not establish authorization.
optionExplanations.D: That weakens the target boundary.

questions.stem: The plan's subscription is not the intended learning subscription. What should the learner do?

options.A: Apply because a resource group is inexpensive.
options.B: Stop and reconcile input, CLI context, and provider target.
options.C: Rename the plan file to safe.tfplan.
options.D: Hide the subscription line from review.

optionExplanations.A: Low cost does not authorize another subscription.
optionExplanations.B: Target mismatch must be resolved before apply.
optionExplanations.C: A filename does not alter its target.
optionExplanations.D: That removes important evidence.

questions.stem: Why does this simple resource-group lesson still recommend protecting local Terraform artifacts?

options.A: Every plan is automatically encrypted by Terraform.
options.B: State contains only formatting preferences.
options.C: Later plans and state can hold sensitive deployment data.
options.D: Only source files matter for security.

optionExplanations.A: Local artifacts are not inherently encrypted.
optionExplanations.B: It records object bindings and attributes.
optionExplanations.C: Safe artifact habits should start before secrets are introduced.
optionExplanations.D: Generated artifacts can also expose data.

questions.stem: The cleanup script needs the resource-group name without surrounding quotation marks. Which command is appropriate?

options.A: terraform output -json resource_group_name
options.B: terraform fmt resource_group_name
options.C: az account show --query name

optionExplanations.A: JSON output retains JSON encoding.
optionExplanations.B: Formatting does not fetch values.
optionExplanations.C: That returns a subscription/account field, not this group output.
optionExplanations.D: -raw prints a scalar value for shell use.

questions.stem: Why capture the resource-group name before terraform destroy?

options.A: The output may disappear after its resource is removed.
options.B: Destroy needs an output to rename the subscription.
options.C: The name stops Azure billing without deletion.
options.D: State outputs survive every destroy unchanged.

optionExplanations.A: The saved name enables the independent existence check.
optionExplanations.B: It does not rename subscriptions.
optionExplanations.C: A local variable is not a billing control.
optionExplanations.D: Outputs depending on removed resources need not remain.

questions.stem: Which pair of results matches the documented successful cleanup?

options.A: Empty state alone while Azure says true.
options.B: Empty managed state and az group exists returning false.
options.C: A false tag query with the group still present.
options.D: A successful formatting check and unchanged Azure group.

optionExplanations.A: An orphaned group may remain.
optionExplanations.B: It combines Terraform inventory with Azure readback.
optionExplanations.C: Missing tags do not prove deletion.
optionExplanations.D: Formatting is not cleanup verification.

sources.title: Manage resource groups with Azure CLI

questions.stem: A learner deletes tfplan and assumes the group is gone. What is correct?

options.A: The group disappears when its plan is removed.
options.B: Terraform automatically purges Azure at terminal exit.
options.C: Deleting the plan file does not delete the Azure resource.

optionExplanations.A: Plan files do not control object lifetime after apply.
optionExplanations.B: Managed resources persist beyond the shell.
optionExplanations.C: A reviewed destroy operation is still required.
optionExplanations.D: That removes local runtime data, not Azure objects.

questions.stem: What is the purpose of features {} in the supplied AzureRM provider block?

options.A: It declares an Azure resource group.
options.B: It chooses a VM image.
options.C: It stores the administrator password.
options.D: It is provider configuration required by this provider's setup.

optionExplanations.A: The group has a separate resource block.
optionExplanations.B: There is no VM in this lesson.
optionExplanations.C: No password is generated here.
optionExplanations.D: It is not an Azure resource declaration.

questions.stem: Why run the commands from CLZ-120-terraform-core-workflow?

options.A: Terraform evaluates that root module and its state context.
options.B: The folder title grants Contributor.
options.C: Every folder shares one mandatory state file.
options.D: Azure accepts only commands from that path.

optionExplanations.A: Working in another folder may target different resources.
optionExplanations.B: Folder names do not grant RBAC.
optionExplanations.C: These standalone lessons have their own context.
optionExplanations.D: Azure does not enforce local repository paths.

questions.stem: terraform validate succeeds but plan fails to authenticate. Why is that possible?

options.A: Validate always checks active Azure login.
options.B: Validation checks configuration consistency; planning may contact Azure.
options.C: A successful validate guarantees Azure availability.

optionExplanations.A: It does not validate live authorization.
optionExplanations.B: These commands test different boundaries.
optionExplanations.C: It is not a service availability test.
optionExplanations.D: The Azure provider needs credentials for remote reads/actions.

questions.stem: Which four metadata keys are applied by the supplied local.tags map?

options.A: Owner, Password, Token, and Secret.
options.B: CPU, RAM, Disk, and NIC.
options.C: Project, Environment, ManagedBy, and Lab.

optionExplanations.A: Those are not the supplied keys and secrets do not belong in tags.
optionExplanations.B: Those are not this metadata map.
optionExplanations.C: They are the standard ownership/context tags.
optionExplanations.D: No such tag map is declared.

questions.stem: Only an added Owner tag changes while the group's name and location remain fixed. What should the learner inspect?

options.A: A mandatory redeployment of every Azure service.
options.B: A new CLI login for each tag key.
options.C: An automatic state migration.
options.D: The plan for the intended metadata update.

optionExplanations.A: The module manages just one group.
optionExplanations.B: Tags do not define authentication.
optionExplanations.C: No backend change follows from a tag addition.
optionExplanations.D: Review confirms the scope and any unexpected actions.

questions.stem: Why is terraform show tfplan part of the workflow before apply?

options.A: To review intended actions and target context.
options.B: To make all destructive actions safe automatically.
options.C: To change provider credentials stored in the file.
options.D: To create the group without apply.

optionExplanations.A: A saved plan is still a proposal requiring inspection.
optionExplanations.B: Displaying a plan does not remove risk.
optionExplanations.C: Show is inspection, not credential editing.
optionExplanations.D: Show does not execute changes.

questions.stem: The resource group's name references local.prefix. Where is that value computed?

options.A: By Azure billing.
options.B: In the module's local expressions.
options.C: From the resource_group_name output.

optionExplanations.A: Billing does not generate this prefix.
optionExplanations.B: The resource consumes a derived naming expression.
optionExplanations.C: The output exposes the resource result; it does not define local.prefix.
optionExplanations.D: No VM is declared.

questions.stem: Which change fits CLZ-120's Production Delta for team use?

options.A: Commit terraform.tfstate to public GitHub.
options.B: Let each teammate edit the same state JSON by hand.
options.C: A reviewed remote backend with locking and recovery controls.

optionExplanations.A: That publishes operational data.
optionExplanations.B: Manual concurrent edits risk corruption.
optionExplanations.C: Local teaching state is not the final shared-state design.
optionExplanations.D: That removes protection against concurrent writes.

questions.stem: For production CI, which authentication approach does this lesson recommend?

options.A: A personal access token pasted into Terraform locals.
options.B: An anonymous Azure deployment.
options.C: The website progress key as a credential.
options.D: Workload identity federation with reviewed plan/apply control.

optionExplanations.A: That is not an Azure workload identity design.
optionExplanations.B: Azure requires an authorized identity.
optionExplanations.C: Browser progress is not authentication.
optionExplanations.D: It avoids long-lived embedded secrets.

questions.stem: After editing inputs, should the learner apply a tfplan made before those edits as if it reflects them?

options.A: No; produce and inspect a new plan for the new intent.
options.B: Yes, saved plans always reread every changed input.
options.C: Only changing its filename is necessary.
options.D: The old plan automatically includes portal edits.

optionExplanations.A: A saved plan records the inputs/actions from its generation.
optionExplanations.B: Applying a saved plan uses its recorded proposal.
optionExplanations.C: Renaming does not update the plan.
optionExplanations.D: Changes require fresh review and may invalidate assumptions.

questions.stem: Someone placed an unrelated resource in the lab group. What should happen before approving destruction?

options.A: Delete it because the group has a Lab tag.
options.B: Stop and resolve the unrelated resource's ownership.
options.C: Remove state so nothing can be deleted.

optionExplanations.A: A tag does not prove ownership of every contained object.
optionExplanations.B: Group deletion can affect everything inside the boundary.
optionExplanations.C: That can orphan managed infrastructure.
optionExplanations.D: Review is essential when the boundary changed.
